patient.name: Daniel Reyes
patient.chiefComplaint: Fall from scaffolding, severe pelvic and lower back pain

history.hpi: Roofing contractor fell approximately 25 feet from scaffolding onto packed dirt, landing feet-first then falling backward. Coworkers report he was briefly stunned but did not lose consciousness. Complains of severe pelvic pain and inability to stand. Denies neck pain but reports diffuse lower back tenderness.
history.events: Scaffolding plank gave way; coworkers called 911 immediately and kept him still on the ground

scene.dispatch: 48-year-old male, fall from height, construction site
scene.location: Residential construction site, patient supine on packed dirt at the base of a two-story scaffold
scene.safety: Scaffold has been secured by site foreman; hard hat area, crew directing bystanders back
scene.bystanders: Two coworkers present, witnessed the fall, kept patient still per 911 dispatcher instructions
visualCues: Patient supine on dirt, scaffold visible above at estimated 25-foot height
Pelvis appears asymmetric with bruising over both iliac crests
Patient guarding pelvis, unwilling to move legs
Hard hat cracked but still on patient's head

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 48-year-old male supine at the base of a scaffold, alert and in severe pain, with bruising and asymmetry over the pelvis. He denies neck pain but reports diffuse back and pelvic pain.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present but thready, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and movement intact in all four extremities, guarding pelvis
otherFindings: Pelvic pain 9/10, worse with any movement
Bruising and asymmetry noted over bilateral iliac crests
Diffuse lower back tenderness, no midline point tenderness
Denies neck pain, denies loss of consciousness
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "My hips feel like they're crushed — please don't move me."

transitions.if: Primary survey and pelvic binder applied
transitions.condition: Crew performs a MARCH primary survey, palpates the pelvis once for instability, applies a pelvic binder, and initiates spinal motion restriction given the high-risk fall mechanism and distracting pelvic injury.

phases.name: Primary survey and pelvic binder applied
phases.description: Crew completes the MARCH primary survey, palpates the pelvis once for instability, applies a pelvic binder, initiates spinal motion restriction given the fall greater than 10 feet, and establishes IV access for fluid resuscitation.
phases.triggerCondition: After the primary survey confirms no massive hemorrhage or airway compromise, the crew recognizes pelvic instability on a single gentle palpation and the fall-from-height mechanism (greater than 10 feet) as criteria for pelvic binder application and spinal motion restriction, and establishes IV access given hypotension and tachycardia.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, thready, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and movement intact distal to pelvis in all four extremities
otherFindings: Pelvic binder applied at level of greater trochanters
Cervical collar applied for spinal motion restriction
No midline spinal tenderness on palpation

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform MARCH primary survey: hemorrhage, airway, breathing, circulation, head/hypothermia
expectedActions.rationale: Rules out other life threats before focusing on the obvious pelvic injury.

expectedActions.shortAction: Palpate pelvis ONCE by applying medial pressure on iliac crests bilaterally to assess instability
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Pelvis: Palpate once for instability by applying medial pressure on the iliac crests bilaterally
expectedActions.rationale: A single gentle palpation assesses instability without dislodging a forming clot.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply pelvic binder to stabilize suspected unstable pelvis
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If pelvis is unstable, place pelvic binder or sheet to stabilize pelvis
expectedActions.rationale: Stabilizing the pelvic ring reduces ongoing venous and bony hemorrhage.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply cervical collar and initiate spinal motion restriction for fall >10 feet
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Mechanisms that have been associated with a higher risk of injury are: Falls greater than 10 feet
expectedActions.rationale: A 25-foot fall is a high-risk mechanism warranting spinal motion restriction even without neck complaints.

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish large-bore IV access given SBP <90 and HR >120
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access if needed (large bore preferred)
expectedActions.rationale: Vascular access is required before fluid resuscitation can begin for this hypotensive, tachycardic patient.

transitions.condition: With IV access established and SBP persistently less than 90 mmHg, the crew initiates a 500 mL crystalloid bolus targeting an SBP of 90 mmHg.
Instead of palpating once and moving on, the crew repeatedly presses on the pelvis to 'recheck' stability, risking dislodgement of a forming clot and worsening hemorrhage.

phases.name: Fluid bolus given for shock
phases.description: A 500 mL crystalloid bolus is given for persistent hypotension. Blood pressure improves toward the trauma resuscitation target, and the patient receives weight-based analgesia before transport.
phases.triggerCondition: SBP remains below 90 mmHg after pelvic binder placement, meeting criteria for crystalloid fluid resuscitation targeting SBP 90 mmHg.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses stronger, skin still cool but less diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and movement intact distal to pelvis in all four extremities
otherFindings: Fentanyl 90 mcg IV given for pain (90 kg x 1 mcg/kg)
Pelvic binder and cervical collar remain in place
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Okay, that's a bit more bearable now."

expectedActions.shortAction: 500 mL crystalloid bolus IV, reassess SBP, repeat as needed (target SBP 90 mmHg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If SBP less than 90 mmHg or HR greater than 120 BPM, initiate resuscitation: ... consider 500 mL bolus of IV fluid, repeat as needed for persistent signs and symptoms of shock ... Trauma resuscitation target SBP 90 mmHg (palpable radial pulse or alert mental status). Reassess SBP after bolus given
expectedActions.rationale: Titrated crystalloid resuscitation restores perfusion without over-diluting clotting factors.

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 90 mcg IV (90 kg x 1 mcg/kg = 90 mcg; max initial dose 100 mcg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg)
expectedActions.rationale: Weight-based fentanyl provides rapid analgesia for a patient with a severe pelvic injury.

transitions.condition: SBP rises toward the 90 mmHg target and heart rate trends down; patient is packaged for rapid transport to the appropriate trauma center.

phases.name: Perfusion improved, prepared for transport
phases.description: Patient is packaged with pelvic binder and cervical collar in place, perfusion trending toward target, and transported to a trauma center with serial vital sign reassessment.
phases.triggerCondition: After fluid resuscitation and analgesia, SBP trends toward 90 mmHg and the patient is packaged for rapid transport, minimizing scene time given the high-risk mechanism and ongoing shock physiology.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses strong, skin warming, less pale
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and movement intact distal to pelvis in all four extremities
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Thank you, I know this looks bad."

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs and pelvic binder position serially en route to trauma center
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Monitor patient for deterioration over time with serial vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) and repeat neurologic status assessment
expectedActions.rationale: Pelvic fractures can continue to bleed occultly even after initial improvement with fluids.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to appropriate trauma center per field triage guideline; minimize scene time
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Decisions regarding transport destination should be based on the ACS-COT 2022 National Guideline for the Field Triage of Injured Patients
expectedActions.rationale: A high-risk fall with hemodynamic instability requires the highest level of trauma care available.

phases.name: Pelvis palpated repeatedly to reassess
phases.description: The crew repeatedly presses on the pelvis to 'recheck' instability instead of palpating once, risking dislodgement of a forming clot. The patient's pain and hemodynamic status worsen.
phases.triggerCondition: Instead of a single gentle palpation, the crew presses on the pelvis multiple times to reassess stability, which can disrupt an early clot and worsen ongoing pelvic hemorrhage.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weaker and more thready, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and movement intact distal to pelvis in all four extremities
otherFindings: Increased pelvic pain and guarding after repeated palpation
Patient anxious, repeatedly asking crew to stop touching his hips
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Stop pushing on it, please, it's getting worse!"

expectedActions.shortAction: Stop repeat pelvic palpation, apply binder immediately, and begin fluid resuscitation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Pelvis: Palpate once for instability by applying medial pressure on the iliac crests bilaterally
expectedActions.rationale: Repeated pelvic palpation can worsen bony and venous hemorrhage; stabilize and treat the shock it caused instead of continuing to reassess.
